name: battery_charging
description: Use when the car cranks slowly, will not start, the battery light flickers or the battery keeps going flat: battery, cranking and charging under load.
instructions: Call run_skill {"name":"battery_charging"}: it runs the battery capture (the driver restarts the engine: resting voltage, cranking dip, charging), then asks the driver to switch on the headlights, A/C and rear demister, reads the voltage and rpm for 5 s and asks for them to be switched off.
Read the battery verdict and the under-load line; a part the digest says was not judged (the driver could not do it, the engine was not running) is no evidence either way.
For a battery that goes flat overnight, also open alerts_history (low-voltage alerts) and maintenance (battery age) when they are offered.
interpret: Resting voltage (engine off): about 12.6 V is fully charged; under 12.2 V the battery is discharged.
Cranking dip under 9.6 V: a weak battery, or a cable or starter drawing too much.
With the engine running, a module voltage under 13.5 V = not charging.

Under electrical load (lights, A/C, demister) the voltage may sag a little but should stay at or above 13.2 V with the engine running; under 13.2 V points to a worn alternator, a slipping belt or a poor ground or B+ connection.
Over 14.5 V with the engine running is overcharging: the regulator.
A weak battery explains slow cranking, hard starts and random communication codes after a start: settle it before chasing those codes.
